chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd al-Ash'ari al-Qummi, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the person in ihram who buys female slaves and sells them; he said, 'Yes.'

Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And whoever kisses his wife while he is in ihram, upon him is a camel, whether he ejaculated or not; if the woman desired that, it is upon her like what is upon him.
The mention of that has already passed; and whoever kisses his wife, upon him is a camel; if she also desired that, it is upon her also a camel. He narrated that.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.بَدَنَةٌ: A camel, used here as the specific monetary/animal expiation penalty

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for kissing one's wife while in the state of ihram during Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that the penalty of a *badanah* (a camel) for kissing one's spouse while in *ihram* applies regardless of ejaculation, emphasizing the act itself as the trigger. It further establishes the principle of mutual liability, noting that if the wife desires the intimacy, she incurs the same penalty, reflecting the Shia juristic view on shared responsibility in ritual violations. The text also briefly mentions the permissibility of a pilgrim buying and selling female slaves, highlighting the flexibility of commercial transactions during the sacred state.
